'''Paolo Gorini''' (18 January 1813 – 2 February 1881) was an [[Italians|Italian]] [[mathematician]], [[professor]], [[scientist]], and [[politician]]<ref name="Treccani">{{cite encyclopedia |last=Conti |first=Fulvio |year=2002 |title=GORINI, Paolo |url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/paolo-gorini_(Dizionario-Biografico)/ |language=it |encyclopedia=[[Enciclopedia Treccani]] |location=[[Rome]] |publisher=Treccani |series=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani |volume=58 |access-date=19 December 2021}}</ref> renowned as a pioneer of [[cremation]] in [[Europe]], primarily in the [[United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland|United Kingdom]].<ref name="Treccani"/>

==Biography==
Born in [[Pavia]], Gorini obtained a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Pavia]] in 1832 and subsequently moved to [[Lodi, Lombardy|Lodi]] in 1834, where he worked as [[lecturer]] of [[physics]] in the local lyceum.<ref name="Treccani"/> There he achieved noteworthy discoveries about [[Organic compound|organic]] substances.<ref name="Treccani"/> Gorini became interested in [[politics]] at a very young age and joined the emerging [[Risorgimento|Italian nationalist movement]] during the [[First Italian War of Independence]].<ref name="Treccani"/>

After the [[Five Days of Milan]] (1848), he fled to [[Switzerland]] and was further exiled to [[London]], [[England]], where he continued his eclectic studies in [[natural sciences]] ([[anatomy]], [[biology]], [[chemistry]], [[geology]], and [[physiology]]).<ref name="Treccani"/> Back in Lodi, in 1871, he published ''Sull'origine del vulcani'' ("On the Origin of Volcanoes") and, in 1872, he became famous for the [[embalming]] of the bodies of [[Giuseppe Mazzini]] and [[Giuseppe Rovani]].<ref name="Treccani"/><ref name="Podgorny 2012">{{cite journal |author-last=Podgorny |author-first=Irina |date=January 2012 |title=Changing the Dead to Statues of Stone: The Synthesis of Fossils, Petrifaction, Photography, and the Chemistry of the Gorgonean Arts |journal=[[Nuncius (journal)|Nuncius: Journal of the Material and Visual History of Science]] |location=[[Leiden]] |publisher=[[Brill Publishers]] |volume=27 |issue=2: ''Immortal Bodies'' |pages=289–308 |doi=10.1163/18253911-02702004 |issn=1825-3911}}</ref>

In 1878, he was commissioned by the [[Cremation Society of Great Britain]] to construct the cremator at [[Woking Crematorium]] in England. He died in Lodi in 1881; following a [[Civil funeral|civil ceremony]], his remains were [[Cremation|cremated]] and buried in the local cemetery of Riolo.<ref name="Treccani"/> A monument and a museum are dedicated to him in Lodi.<ref>AA. VV, ''Paolo Gorini. Scienziato a Lodi nell'800'', cd rom, Provincia di Lodi, Lodi 1999</ref> In 2021, the [[documentary film]] ''Il mago di Lodi'' ("The wizard of Lodi") dedicated to his life and works as [[embalmer]] was directed by Silvia Onegli and produced by Magestic Film.
